- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Semana Santa is a religious festival where processions of elaborately decorated floats depicting scenes from the Passion of Christ are carried through the streets by members of the city's religious brotherhoods.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] People gather in the streets to watch the processions, and many families have their own traditions and rituals associated with the festival, such as attending particular processions or visiting specific churches.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Feria de Abril is a week-long festival that takes place two weeks after Semana Santa.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Feria de Abril is a celebration of Andalusian culture, with lots of dancing, music, food, and drink.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The festival is held in a large fairground on the outskirts of the city, with huge marquees, or casetas, set up by families, businesses, and social clubs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The casetas are brightly decorated and offer food and drink to visitors.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Flamenco dancers and musicians provide entertainment during Feria de Abril.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, Semana Santa and Feria de Abril are celebrated with great passion and pride in Sevilla, as times of joy and celebration.
